rationale: The first round studies reductions only because the gate placed the candidate rules inside the existing grammar.
A finite interface is one way a bound on consequential local information could show up.
Closure of the reduced chain is the grammar question attached to an exact interface.
A positive defect is a witness that the external signature is not predictively sufficient.
Neighbour sizes are how a claimed six-node distinction would have to be seen.
Composition is the same interface question asked of two designated structures at once.
The item budget decides which of these reductions can actually be calculated.
Propagation along a path index is a different size question from the number of nodes inside one structure.
Behaviour that the named questions do not classify is still part of the coherence map.
